panels.description: Open client connections per Envoy instance, and the rate of new connections. A flat active line with a rising accept rate means connections are being closed as fast as they arrive.
panels.title: Downstream connections

panels.description: Connections Envoy refused before any routing happened. Non-zero cx_overflow means a listener or global connection limit is capping the load balancer, not the backends.
panels.title: Connection rejections (listener)

panels.description: Envoy's own self-protection. Heap pressure approaching 1 or any active overload action means Envoy is already shedding load: it will stop accepting requests/connections before it OOMs.
panels.title: Overload manager

panels.description: Requests waiting for a free upstream connection. This is the clearest early sign that backends are the bottleneck: it rises well before latency or errors do.
panels.title: Upstream queue depth (pending requests)

panels.description: 1 means that circuit breaker is tripped and Envoy is rejecting work for that upstream cluster right now. Which one opens tells you the limit to raise: cx, rq_pending, rq or rq_retry.
panels.title: Circuit breakers open

panels.description: How much of each budget is left before the breaker trips. A value trending to 0 is the warning that the panel to its left is about to go to 1.
panels.title: Circuit breaker headroom

panels.description: Work Envoy dropped itself rather than passing upstream. Any of these is user-visible failure caused by a limit in Envoy's own configuration.
panels.title: Load shed by Envoy

panels.description: Concurrent requests being served downstream, and requests started per second. Divergence between the two means requests are taking longer to complete.
panels.title: Requests in flight

panels.description: Open upstream connections divided by healthy hosts. A sharp climb here while request rate is flat means connections are piling up because backends are answering more slowly.
panels.title: Upstream connections per healthy host

panels.description: End-to-end latency as the client sees it, including time queued inside Envoy.
panels.title: Downstream request duration

panels.description: Backend-side latency per upstream cluster. Compare with the panel to the left to see whether slowness originates upstream or inside Envoy.
panels.title: Upstream request duration p99 by cluster

panels.description: Downstream p99 minus upstream p99: the latency Envoy itself adds, mostly connection-pool queueing. If this grows while upstream p99 is flat, the load balancer is the bottleneck.
panels.title: Time spent inside Envoy (p99)

panels.description: TCP/TLS connect time to backends. A spike here with healthy request latency points at the network, conntrack tables or backend accept queues rather than application code.
panels.title: Upstream connect time p99

panels.description: Bytes moved downstream (received positive, sent negative) per Envoy instance. Useful for spotting a single instance carrying a disproportionate share of traffic.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Traffic split across load balancer instances. A persistent imbalance means the layer in front of Envoy (DNS, cloud LB, keepalive reuse) is not spreading load evenly.
panels.title: Request rate per Envoy instance

panels.description: Response codes returned to clients, stacked. Envoy's own rejections (503 on circuit breaker, 429 on rate limit) show up here as 5xx/4xx even when backends are fine.
panels.title: Downstream responses by class

panels.description: Server errors as a share of all responses. Threshold lines at 1% and 5%.
panels.title: Downstream 5xx ratio

panels.description: Which backend cluster is producing the errors.
panels.title: Upstream 5xx by cluster

panels.description: Failures reaching or completing against backends. connect_timeout and rq_timeout separate 'cannot open a connection' from 'connection opened but the response never came'.
panels.title: Upstream connection and request failures

panels.description: Retries amplify load on an already-struggling backend. retry_overflow means the retry budget is exhausted and requests are failing without a second attempt.
panels.title: Retries

panels.description: Stream resets and handshake failures. A rise in downstream protocol errors or TLS errors under load often means clients are timing out and abandoning connections.
panels.title: Resets, protocol and TLS errors

panels.description: Healthy, degraded and total hosts per upstream cluster. Losing hosts concentrates the same traffic on fewer backends, which is a common cause of sudden pressure.
panels.title: Cluster membership

panels.description: Share of each cluster that is currently healthy. Below the panic threshold (50% by default) Envoy stops excluding unhealthy hosts entirely.
panels.title: Healthy host ratio

panels.description: Non-zero means too few healthy hosts remain, so Envoy is load balancing across all hosts including unhealthy ones. Requests will fail while this is firing.
panels.title: LB panic mode

panels.description: Hosts Envoy pulled out of rotation for failing. Ejections shrink the pool and can cascade: each ejection raises load on the hosts that remain.
panels.title: Outlier detection ejections

panels.description: Health check failures and timeouts per cluster, before ejection kicks in.
panels.title: Active health checks

panels.description: New upstream connections per second against destroys. High churn means connections are not being reused, so every request pays connect and TLS cost.
panels.title: Upstream connection churn

panels.description: Allocated vs heap vs physical memory. Allocated tracking heap upward while traffic is flat usually means buffered data from slow backends or slow clients.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: Worker threads that failed to check in on time. This is the strongest signal that Envoy is CPU starved: the event loop is blocked and every request on that worker stalls.
panels.title: Watchdog misses

panels.description: envoy_server_state is 0 when live; anything else means draining, initializing or pre-initializing. total_connections is the process-wide count the global connection limit applies to.
panels.title: Server state and connections

panels.description: A resetting uptime means the process restarted; a rising hot restart epoch means a config reload swapped the binary. Both explain sudden metric discontinuities elsewhere on this dashboard.
panels.title: Uptime and hot restarts

panels.description: connected_state 0 means Envoy has lost its control plane and is serving the last config it received. Update failures mean new config is being rejected.
panels.title: xDS control plane

panels.description: Minimum days to expiry across all configured TLS certificates.
panels.title: Days until first certificate expires
